executiveSummary: GM1731 Midden-Drenthe was the next pending manifest entry after excluding claimed GM0086 and GM0088, and its artifact was absent immediately before claim. The official/generated 2025 identity, 34,021 residents, 48 neighbourhoods in seventeen districts, 25 BAG woonplaatsen, 38 settlement labels and ten logical road-border records are coherent. Neighbourhood rows total 33,990 residents, 31 below the municipality control (-0.091%); the allocator reconciles independent CBS rounding without changing published values. All ten presets run deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services with bounded values, service-layer-invariant hazard, exact no-event behavior, causal-ledger closure and monotone event-attributable burden. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The municipality's adopted climate strategy says it has no specific overstromingen assignment, consistent with exact-zero direct coastal and Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing, but not with an all-water all-clear: local evidence identifies Beilerstroom, Beilervaart, Linthorst-Homankanaal, Drentsche Hoofdvaart, groundwater, sewers and named rain hotspots. The pluvial preset publishes 0.545863 normalized inundation stress at T+24 without those mechanisms, and severe storm publishes 0.467513. Seven materially different nonzero T+24 hazard families reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood order; documented Brunsting, Westerbork and Hooghalen rain attention areas rank 28th, 22nd and 18th of 48. The canonical wildfire produces zero direct fire and only remote smoke despite extensive wooded/heath/recreation exposure; a controlled ignition in Verspreide huizen Spier leaves the source neighbourhood 40th of 48. Most importantly, KNMI and the municipality document a magnitude 3.0 induced earthquake at Geelbroek by the Eleveld gas field on 14 March 2026, an M1.3 aftershock, prior felt events and possible Midden-Drenthe building damage. The simulator instead uses an unbound fixed Groningen source and reports 0.072141 g at T+6. A zero in-boundary event-origin count in the deployment snapshot proves point-containment coverage is insufficient, not zero shaking. Beilen station, the A28, N381 and 93 scheduled stop areas are important but static; a future N381/A28-junction closure and a June 2026 storm/rail incident illustrate time-valid dependency without proving scenario state. There is no in-boundary RIVM SEH; external Assen, Hoogeveen and Emmen roles require destination- and time-specific routing. Partial public context contains 247 water objects, one Beilen grid-planning sample, one KNMI observation station, 145 antennas and 25 education locations. Enexis separately reports current structural Beilen congestion, but planning capacity is not outage resilience. Attero and the Wijster Energy Transition Park add industrial, waste, odor/air and transport pathways omitted by the ten presets. Drenthe's 2026 emergency-support-point work is a Westerveld pilot; no reviewed source confirms a Midden-Drenthe site, capacity, stock or activation. Unknown lifeline, visitor, industrial, care and response state remains Unknown or NoData, never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1731 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated CBS/BAG/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; audited 3 September 2026
supports: The official/generated row identifies GM1731 as Midden-Drenthe and reports 34,021 residents, density 100/km², 26.3% aged 65-plus and 4,639 one-person households. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and supplies static aggregate context, not incident occupancy or individual vulnerability.

The municipality reference point [6.5436689877255985,52.85956909561097] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary. The outline supports administrative selection and aggregation, not water, sewer, road, rail, nature-fire, care or utility connectivity.

Forty-eight neighbourhood rows in seventeen districts sum to 33,990 residents (-31, -0.091%), 15,040 households and 8,975 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. Model reconciliation preserves the source rows.

BAG supplies 25 active woonplaatsen and BRT supplies 38 locality labels. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT is CC BY 4.0; woonplaats geometry, settlement labels and demographic provenance remain distinct.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Adopted Local Adaptation Strategy and Implementation Agenda 2022–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Dated 22 December 2022; amended strategy adopted unanimously 20 April 2023 for 2022–2027; no standard reuse licence found
supports: The strategy identifies water nuisance, drought and heat as the three relevant municipal climate themes and states the climate atlas shows no specific overstromingen assignment inside Midden-Drenthe. That is planning context, not an incident all-clear.

Its implementation agenda names Brunstingerstraat in Beilen, Borkerhout and Steffensberg in Westerbork, and Hooghalen as water-nuisance attention locations. It also treats resident communication for extreme weather and water/sewer projects as ongoing work rather than completed protection.

The underlying stress test and adaptation horizon describe scenarios and future resilience. They do not provide a current rainfall observation, selected event, street-level hydraulic forecast, live sewer state, exact local depth/stress, arrival or recession.
Official zero/not-applicable for primary/coastal or named major-river forcing must remain distinct from pluvial, groundwater, brook/canal, sewer and indirect evacuation/logistics effects.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Drents Overijsselse Delta / Noorderzijlvest / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Beilervaart, Beilerstroom, Drenthe canal and partial water-control context
evidenceSources.edition: WDODelta Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027 and Beilervaart project current July 2026–early 2027; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: WDODelta describes the Beilervaart as connecting the Drentsche Hoofdvaart to the Linthorst-Homankanaal at Beilen and is dredging thirteen kilometres in 2026–2027 so the canal can drain during wet periods and retain water during drought. Construction planning is not a current failure or forecast.

WDODelta records that low parts of Lievingerveld in the Beilerstroom valley experienced high-water nuisance in 2021 and can do so again during heavy rain; conditions preserve water storage, slot drainage and pile construction. This is a local pathway absent from a single municipality stress scalar.

The regional programme distinguishes Oude Vaart, Wold Aa, Oude Diep, Drenthe canals and Meppelerdiep systems, wet discharge toward IJsselmeer and dry-period pumping from Meppel. Noorderzijlvest separately governs part of the Smilde area. Boundaries and cross-water-board control matter.

The partial CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH assignment contains 247 points: 194 weirs, 28 surface-water pumps, four sluices, nineteen sewer pumps and two wastewater plants at Beilen and Smilde. These points do not prove completeness, compatible capacities, connectivity, telemetry, live operation, power/backup or restoration; null remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Drenthe / Provincie Drenthe / Brandweer Nederland
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025 and nature/recreation risk context
evidenceSources.edition: VRD Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025 with published amendments; current public copy inspected 3 September 2026; no standard reuse licence found
supports: VRD distinguishes long rain with saturated systems/high groundwater and limited discharge, 70 mm/hour urban cloudbursts, brook/canal overtopping and road closure. Drenthe has no primary sea/river defences; direct high-water concern from IJssel/Overijsselse Vecht concentrates around Meppel, while Drenthe may receive evacuees and indirect lifeline disruption.

VRD identifies storm road blockage, water-utility repair and cascading power, drinking-water, ICT/telecom and care effects. It explicitly treats risk analysis as qualitative/partner-informed rather than precise municipal prediction.

VRD identifies nature fire as a major concern because nature areas contain recreation grounds, care institutions and vital infrastructure and because tourists, camp owners and residents require self-reliance planning. Drenthe's fire service is predominantly volunteer-based, so static post locations do not establish concurrent incident capacity.

Provincial primary sources identify Dwingelderveld, Mantingerzand/Mantingerveld and other forest/heath/wet-heath systems in or bordering Midden-Drenthe. Current regional nature-fire phase is a timestamped regional observation, not a T+72 ignition or spread forecast.

evidenceSources.publisher: Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut / Gemeente Midden-Drenthe
evidenceSources.title: E05 — 14 March 2026 Eleveld/Geelbroek induced earthquake and damage semantics
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI event and analysis published March 2026; municipal damage page current 3 September 2026; KNMI public data CC BY 4.0
supports: KNMI records an induced magnitude 3.0 earthquake at Geelbroek near the Eleveld gas field at 02:14 on 14 March 2026 and an M1.3 aftershock at 05:12. Many people felt it, and earlier felt events occurred near Eleveld in October 2023.

KNMI's technical analysis says 52 other measured earthquakes occurred in and around Eleveld since 1986, while newer events have lower location uncertainty and lie over the field or its boundary faults. Event origin, measured motion and consequence are separate evidence classes.

The municipality states residents of Midden-Drenthe may have sustained building damage and routes reports through the Commissie Mijnbouwschade; acute safety concerns use the competent damage/safety channel. This does not establish that every building is damaged or unsafe.

The deployed 365-day point snapshot assigns zero event origins inside the generalized GM1731 polygon, even though the documented nearby event affected its residents. Polygon origin absence is therefore NoData for source containment, not zero shaking, zero damage or safety.

evidenceSources.publisher: Provincie Drenthe / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / RIVM / Wilhelmina Ziekenhuis Assen / Treant
evidenceSources.title: E06 — A28/N381/rail/bus and external acute-care dependency
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail, OVapi and RIVM snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; operator/current pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Ten CC0 logical boundary records cover the A28, N381, N371, N373, N374 and N855 to Assen, Coevorden, Ooststellingwerf, Westerveld, Hoogeveen, Noordenveld and Aa en Hunze. Their 260/150 values are generalized scenario units, and repeated sides of one corridor are series/shared rather than additive capacity.

The province identifies N381 as Drachten–Emmen and announced a 21 September–16 October 2026 closure between Beilen Noord and Hoogersmilde, including N381 connections to A28. At audit time this is a future valid-time restriction, not a current or arbitrary-scenario closure.

ProRail identifies Beilen station; a June 2026 storm account shows a tree/broken overhead-line intervention near Beilen, and historic planned works used replacement buses and closed crossings. Ninety-three GTFS stop areas are schedule context. None establishes scenario-time train/bus operation, capacity, closure, alternatives or restoration.

RIVM v1.1 contains no SEH questionnaire point inside GM1731. WZA Assen has a 24/7 SEH and Treant distinguishes weekday limited non-life-threatening care in Hoogeveen from 24/7 complex SEH care in Emmen. The appropriate destination depends on incident, time, referral, route, acceptance and capacity and must not be guessed.

evidenceSources.publisher: Enexis Netbeheer / WMD Drinkwater / Netbeheer Nederland / KNMI / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Beilen electricity, strategic groundwater and deployment-cached operational-context evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Enexis report published 23 April 2026; municipal/WMD source documents current through 2026; public-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: Enexis reports structural withdrawal congestion in Beilen MST Netdeel 3 affecting parts of Midden-Drenthe, Coevorden and Aa en Hunze: 10.3 MW requested versus 7.8 MW available, no new-request capacity from congestion management, and expected network reinforcement by end 2028 dependent on TenneT. Congestion is not a blackout or emergency reserve measurement.

The one NBNL sample for service area BL Beilen reports 172.8 MW existing, 68/75.6 MW required withdrawal/injection, 18.2/70.9 MW queues, 29/35 requests and nine projects. The open-data product's exact licence identifier was not found; one postcode lookup is not full municipal topology or live state.

Municipal/WMD documents identify Beilen as a strategic groundwater/drinking-water location with monitored source quality and planned capacity. Source protection and annual planning do not establish pipe connectivity, live pressure/quality, backup, customer outage or T+72 restoration.

The deployed context has one CC BY 4.0 KNMI station observation (Hoogeveen, 2 September 2026 23:30 UTC), 145 RDI antenna installations and 25 CC-Attribution DUO education locations. The weather point is an observation only; antenna and school registers do not establish coverage, backhaul, occupancy, emergency role, backup or restoration.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Midden-Drenthe / Provincie Drenthe / Veiligheidsregio Drenthe
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Wijster industrial/air-quality pathways and Drenthe emergency-support planning
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal ETP page and provincial 2026 notices; VRD Jaarverslag 2025 approved 8 April 2026 and Weerbaar Drenthe programme plan; no standard reuse licence found
supports: The municipality identifies Attero, Green Create, Noblesse Proteins, Scania and other operations at the Energy Transition Park near Wijster and a 24/7 provincial odor-reporting pathway supported by electronic sensors. Odor reports are not automatically toxic exposure or a plume forecast.

Provincial public notices show continuing waste, water-treatment and CO2-liquefaction permitting at Attero Wijster. These are industrial/regulatory context, not proof of present failure, a complete hazardous inventory, live air quality or emergency consequence.

VRD identifies dangerous-goods transport over A/N roads, rail and pipelines, new-energy/chemistry incidents and cascading vital-infrastructure/cyber effects as regional planning issues. The ten canonical presets have no distinct technological release/industrial fire/air-quality family.

VRD's 2025 annual report says the first 2026 noodsteunpunt pilot is in Westerveld; its programme distinguishes cold phase, warm phase within 72 hours, after 72 hours and recovery. No reviewed public source confirms a Midden-Drenthe support point, activation trigger, capacity, staff, stock, generator, water or accessibility.

identity.summary: GM1731, Midden-Drenthe, Drenthe and safety region Drenthe agree across official/generated inputs.
notes: The immutable audits/manifest.json listed GM1731 pending and its artifact was absent immediately before claim; assigned GM0086 and GM0088 were excluded.
Municipality code/name, province, safety-region membership and 2025 editions agree, and the reference point lies inside the boundary.
No identity or municipality-control contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Administrative geometry is coherent, but a large dispersed municipality with multiple water boards, nature areas and infrastructure corridors cannot be represented by one centre.
notes: All 25 BAG woonplaats representative points lie inside the generalized boundary; points do not establish watershed, groundwater, sewer, fire, plume, building or access geometry.
Beilen/Beilerstroom, Smilde/Drentsche Hoofdvaart, Westerbork, Wijster/ETP, Hooghalen/Eleveld and forest/heath/recreation interfaces have different hazard and response pathways.
WDODelta, Noorderzijlvest and Vechtstromen objects appear in the partial assignment, requiring explicit manager/boundary/control provenance rather than municipal-centroid scaling.

demography.summary: The 2025 municipality control and neighbourhood rows reconcile within independent CBS publication rounding.
notes: Official/generated population is 34,021, density 100/km², age65-plus share 26.3% and one-person households 4,639.
Neighbourhood rows total 33,990 (-31, -0.091%), 15,040 households and 8,975 independently rounded age65-plus residents; allocation preserves source observations.
Registered residents exclude nature/recreation visitors, pupils/staff, patients, industrial/agricultural workers, station/road users, responders, transient evacuees and animal populations.

regionalDetail.summary: Core regional rows are strong, while sparse fields and infrastructure registers retain distinct coverage, evidence class and NoData semantics.
notes: All 36 fields are exposed for 48 neighbourhoods; average home value and several housing/benefit fields cover 47/48, cars per household 36/48, and district heat/public charging 0/48. Missing or suppressed publication values are not zero.
The 247 water objects, one NBNL sample, one KNMI observation, 145 antennas and 25 education locations have different publishers, dates, licences, coverage and evidence classes.
The regional rows report 4,315 businesses and 3,423 non-residential buildings, but do not establish shift occupancy, hazardous inventory, process demand, livestock or response priority.

settlements.summary: Twenty-five BAG woonplaatsen and 38 BRT labels preserve dispersion, but not live occupancy, support role or reachability.
notes: Places include Beilen, Smilde, Bovensmilde, Hoogersmilde, Westerbork, Hooghalen, Wijster, Spier, Hijken, Mantinge, Nieuw-Balinge, Orvelte and twelve smaller places; BRT classifies sixteen buurtschappen, two deelkernen, one gehucht and nineteen woonkernen.
The municipality's density of 100/km² and dispersed places create destination-specific road, bus, fire, welfare, water and external-care dependencies.
Nature-park/camp visitors, ETP workers, station users and care populations can differ sharply from registered resident allocation and time of day/season.

transport.summary: A28/N-road proxies, Beilen station and scheduled bus stops cannot support exact emergency access, care, evacuation or supply continuity.
notes: Ten A28/N381/N371/N373/N374/N855 border records include shared physical corridors; their 260/150 values are logical scenario units and non-additive.

Beilen station and 93 GTFS stop areas are static geometry/schedule context; the future N381/A28 connection closure and historical storm/rail disruption demonstrate valid-time state and alternatives, not current closure.

External acute care, volunteer/specialist fire resources, water controls, 25 woonplaatsen, Wijster industry and resupply require time-valid internal/cross-boundary routes, vehicles/crew/fuel and destination acceptance.

emergencyContext.summary: Authorities establish locally material water, fire, induced-seismic, utility, industrial, transport, care and evacuation mechanisms, but not current event/resources.
notes: Direct coastal and named major-river inundation are not the local primary mechanism; separate clocks are required for rain/sewer/groundwater/canal, drought, storm/winter, local fire/smoke, Eleveld seismicity, industrial release, utility/cyber, access, care and reception of external evacuees.
The 26.3% age65-plus share and 4,639 one-person households support aggregate outreach planning, not individual targeting, frailty or self-reliance assumptions.
Drenthe's support-point programme/pilot is not evidence of a confirmed GM1731 incident site or capacity.
Observations, forecasts, scenarios, historic events, current congestion and future works require distinct time/evidence modes and cannot be silently converted to T+0 truth.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1731 pnpm audit:model passed two tests across severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Focused inline Vite runs captured complete T+24/T+72 trajectories, neighbourhood ranks, a local-fire containment probe and the six-checkpoint earthquake path without creating a scratch file.

At T+24 severity / affected people-equivalent / event-attributable person-hours are storm 0.258930 / 12,315 / 209,332.426; pluvial 0.394234 / 6,383 / 164,661.362; river 0 / 0 / 0; coastal 0.011567 / 0 / 8,145.843; heat 0.083903 / 573 / 69,656.733.

These are deterministic exercise indices, modeled people-equivalent and matched-no-event weighted person-hours—not observations, probabilities, casualties, customer outage-hours, economic loss or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation, causal closure and cumulative-burden contracts pass.
notes: All hazards and service availability values remain finite and bounded; affected population, demand, delivery and event-attributable person-hours are non-negative.
Zero-intensity runs have exact zero event hazard, affected population and attributable burden; T+24 repeats are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.
All eight services allocate 48 neighbourhoods and exactly 34,021 residents; demand/delivery reconcile and changing the selected service layer leaves physical hazard unchanged.
Arithmetic validity does not validate local water, wildfire, seismic, industrial, route, care, utility, action or recovery meaning.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Seven unrelated nonzero hazards reuse one complete neighbourhood order and a controlled local wildfire fails source containment.
notes: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have exactly the same nonzero T+24 48-neighbourhood order: Elp, Beilen, Zwiggelte, Bovensmilde-Zuid and Witteveen lead; Smilde-Centrum, Hoogersmilde-Zuid, Verspreide huizen Nieuw-Balinge, Oranje and Orvelte end it.
Official rain attention geography is not recovered: Brunsting ranks 28/48, Westerbork 22/48 and Hooghalen 18/48 under pluvial forcing.

A controlled fire at Verspreide huizen Spier's representative point produces municipal direct-fire intensity 0.278945 and smoke 0.415287, yet the source neighbourhood ranks 40/48 while Elp still leads.
The canonical remote wildfire gives zero direct fire and 0.210196 smoke at T+24; Eleveld shaking, water, heat, fire/plume, cyber target and industrial source each require different coverage geometry.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact water, electricity, telecom, care, mobility, facilities and supply paths lack complete causal topology and live state.
notes: NWB records affect mobility and assumed road supply only, correctly avoiding physical utility equivalence, but route capacity remains a logical proxy and repeated corridor sides remain non-additive.

HWH points do not connect rain/groundwater, canals/brooks, water-board controls, sewers, wastewater plants, strategic WMD groundwater/drinking water, power/backup or quality. Capacity units and completeness are not established.

NBNL/Enexis congestion, RDI, DUO, KNMI, ProRail/GTFS and RIVM/operator care evidence does not supply live outage/load/traffic, full feeder/pipe/backhaul topology, priority, acceptance, occupancy, stock, backup or repair.

At compound T+72 normalized inundation stress remains 0.562686 and availability is power 0.239408, water 0.335841, drainage 0.178136, telecom 0.190564, mobility 0.787165, facilities 0.279750 and supply 0.791840. No operator validates those exact values.

causalTrace.summary: The numerical ledger closes, but event selection, evidence time, local source/destination and accountable actions are absent.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service-stage contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure closes numerically.
Pluvial/storm select no official rain cell, Beilerstroom/Beilervaart/canal boundary, groundwater, sewer or control state; local river/coastal zero is not generalized beyond its named source.

Earthquake selects a fixed Groningen source rather than the documented Eleveld/Geelbroek event and measured motion/vulnerability; wildfire selects a remote source; cyber and industrial effects select no named target/source or detection.

T+0–6 needs event verification/warning; T+6–24 water/fire control, closures, inspection, care routing and support activation; T+24–48 welfare, repair and resupply; T+48–72 verified restoration, re-entry and unresolved-needs review.

recovery72h.summary: Exact recession, recovery, affected-population thresholds and status labels are unsupported by action/resource evidence.
notes: Pluvial stress is 0.545863 at T+24 and exactly zero at T+72 with 403,226.564 person-hours; no selected drainage/control action or measured recession supports that clock.
Heat severity remains 0.083903 at T+72 while affected people-equivalent becomes zero and status operational; no local heat-health observation/action explains this threshold.

Earthquake motion is 0.072141 g at T+6 and zero at T+12, while 3,428 people-equivalent remain affected at T+24; no event-bound inspection, damage, shelter, repair or return action supports the trajectory.

Compound remains critical at T+72 with 0.562686 stress, 21,713 affected people-equivalent and 1,473,566.031 person-hours but no water, utility, access, care, industrial or support action explains the plateau.

findings.summary: The pluvial and storm inundation-stress values are unsupported local hydraulic precision.
findings.evidence: Pluvial publishes 0.545863 and storm 0.467513 normalized inundation stress at T+24. E02/E03 instead supply named urban attention locations, Beilerstroom/Beilervaart/canal/groundwater/sewer mechanisms and multiple water-board controls, but no selected rainfall field, connected raster, live state or recession.
findings.action: Retain the current values only as visibly synthetic stress. Bind an official versioned rain event, terrain/BGT, infiltration, groundwater, sewer, brook/canal boundary, water-board control state, cell footprint, time, uncertainty, licence and NoData before local consequence thresholds are used.

findings.summary: Exact-zero direct coastal and Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing is locally supportable only under narrow source semantics.
findings.evidence: E02 says no specific municipal overstromingen assignment; E04 says Drenthe has no primary sea/river defences and direct high-water concern is around Meppel. The focused gate preserves zero direct river hazard/burden and zero coastal inundation. Local rain, brooks/canals, groundwater, reception of evacuees and indirect lifeline effects remain separate.
findings.action: Retain direct source-specific zero and explicit not-applicable semantics. Regression-test that it never becomes a generic water all-clear or hides indirect storm, transport, utility, care and evacuation-region effects.

findings.summary: Seven hazard families reuse one exact neighbourhood rank that does not recover official rain hotspots.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share all 48 ranks from Elp to Orvelte. Under pluvial, Brunsting is 28th, Westerbork 22nd and Hooghalen 18th despite E02 naming their streets/areas for attention; cyber has no selected target and should not inherit physical water/fire geography.
findings.action: Replace identifier-based scaling with event/source/coverage-aware fields. Require mechanism-specific ranks, source containment, service-layer invariance, official-zero preservation, uncertainty and explicit Unknown outside source coverage.

findings.summary: Remote smoke omits material local direct-fire exposure and local ignition allocation fails containment.
findings.evidence: E04 identifies substantial Drenthe forest/heath, recreation, care and infrastructure exposure. Canonical T+24 produces zero direct fire and smoke 0.210196 from a remote source. A controlled Verspreide huizen Spier ignition produces direct fire 0.278945 and smoke 0.415287 but ranks its source neighbourhood 40/48.
findings.action: Add local ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind/plume, visitor/care occupancy, road/terrain, water and responder-resource inputs. Keep regional fire phase as time-stamped context and remote smoke separate; suppress neighbourhood fire consequences until containment passes.

findings.summary: The earthquake preset ignores the documented Eleveld mechanism and publishes unbound ground motion/consequences.
findings.evidence: E05 documents the 14 March 2026 M3.0 Geelbroek/Eleveld induced event, M1.3 aftershock, prior events and possible GM1731 building damage. The preset instead uses a fixed Groningen source and reports 0.072141 g at T+6, 3,428 affected people-equivalent at T+24 and 304,031.127 person-hours by T+72. Zero assigned in-boundary origins misses cross-boundary shaking.
findings.action: Add event/replay mode using KNMI origin, magnitude/depth/type/revision, measured or modeled ground-motion field and valid time plus governed building/infrastructure vulnerability. Suppress exact consequences without event and vulnerability evidence; show origin containment and shaking coverage separately.

findings.summary: Dispersed settlements, external acute care and Beilen road/rail dependencies are not operationally routed.
findings.evidence: E06 shows no in-boundary RIVM SEH, one Beilen station, 93 scheduled stop areas and ten A28/N-road border proxies. Assen has a 24/7 SEH, Hoogeveen has a weekday basisspoedpost and Emmen handles complex 24/7 acute care; future N381/A28 closure and past rail storm effects require valid-time alternatives.
findings.action: Represent care roles/schedules and incident-confirmed destination/acceptance separately. Add current road, rail and bus state plus internal/cross-boundary routing for 25 places, ambulances, fire, water controls, ETP, support and resupply; shared corridor sides remain non-additive.

findings.summary: Surface-water control, sewer, wastewater and strategic groundwater/drinking water are collapsed into generic Water and Drainage.
findings.evidence: E03 has 247 partial objects across multiple managers and E07 identifies the strategic Beilen groundwater/drinking-water function. These sources do not connect catchments, 194 weirs, 28 surface pumps, four sluices, nineteen sewer pumps, two rwzis, source quality, treatment, pipes, power/backup or live state.
findings.action: Split surface-water level/control, groundwater/source quality, sewer overflow, wastewater treatment and drinking-water quantity/pressure/quality/advisory. Retain manager, status, compatible units, issue/validity and completeness; null and missing topology remain Unknown.

findings.summary: Structural Beilen grid congestion and planning samples do not validate exact outage or recovery trajectories.
findings.evidence: E07 reports a real 10.3 MW requested versus 7.8 MW available congestion condition, no new-request capacity through congestion management and reinforcement expected end 2028 with TenneT dependency. That is transport-capacity planning, not live load, outage, reserve, switching, emergency priority or restoration.
findings.action: Show congestion as a dated planning constraint distinct from incident outage. Bind only authorized time-valid Enexis/TenneT event and aggregate restoration evidence; otherwise keep topology, switching, backup and recovery Unknown and synthetic availability clearly labeled.

findings.summary: Wijster industrial/waste/air and dangerous-goods transport/pipeline pathways lack a selectable scenario.
findings.evidence: E08 identifies multiple ETP operations, odor sensing/reporting, Attero permitting and regional new-energy/chemistry and dangerous-goods road/rail/pipeline risks. None proves present toxic exposure or supplies a complete inventory, but generic wildfire/cyber forcing cannot represent fire, release, plume, odor-versus-toxicity or protective-action decisions.
findings.action: Add an authority-reviewed technological incident mode using public omgevingsveiligheid/permit context and transparent responder-approved envelopes. Keep exact materials, quantities, live facility/pipeline state, plume and security-sensitive topology Unknown unless explicitly published and authorized.

findings.summary: No auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger supports status, recovery or support decisions.
findings.evidence: E08 says Drenthe's first 2026 support-point pilot is in Westerveld, not confirmation of a GM1731 site. The model records no earthquake inspection, water/fire/industrial source control, warning, closure, care route, support activation, welfare check, repair, resupply, completion, verification or rollback.
findings.action: Add proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/blocked/cancelled actions with owner, authority source, issue/valid/expiry, geography, dependencies, resource/capacity, verification and rollback. Cover T+0–6 verification/warning; T+6–24 control/close/inspect/route/activate; T+24–48 welfare/repair/resupply; T+48–72 restoration/re-entry/unresolved needs.

findings.summary: Missing point coverage, sparse publication fields and bounded observations require explicit multi-state rendering.
findings.evidence: District heat/charging cover 0/48 and cars per household 36/48. residualLimitations: This deterministic 72-hour planning stress test is not a Midden-Drenthe, water-board, VRD, KNMI, Enexis, WMD, ProRail, transport, hospital or industrial-operator forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration promise.
No selected local rain field, groundwater state, brook/canal hydrograph, water-board boundary/control state, sewer model, connected footprint, arrival, duration or recession is ingested.

The 0.545863 pluvial and 0.467513 storm flood properties are normalized synthetic inundation stress, not observed or officially modeled metre depths and must not independently drive evacuation, routing, care or service thresholds.

Direct coastal and Rhine/Meuse/IJssel zero applies only to those named sources; it says nothing about rain, brooks/canals, groundwater, sewer, drought, external evacuees or indirect lifeline disruption.
The generalized boundary and reference point do not resolve water systems, terrain, sewers, buildings, roads, rail, nature fuels, industrial sources, facilities, utilities, households or individuals.
CBS values are independently rounded/suppressed; the -31 population difference and missing district-heat/charging/cars/housing fields are publication semantics, not absent/zero people or assets.
HWH is partial and 247 points do not establish complete topology, compatible capacity units, telemetry, live operation, power, backup or restoration; null remains Unknown.
WDODelta dredging and WMD groundwater/capacity plans are planned/current projects, not failures, completed resilience, live quality/pressure or restoration evidence.
No complete public causal Enexis feeder/switching, WMD pipe/treatment, gas district, municipal sewer or telecom backhaul/restoration topology is authorized in the model.
Beilen congestion concerns transport capacity and queues rather than present load, outage, reserve, emergency priority or customer restoration; one NBNL sample is not municipal coverage.
RDI antenna points do not establish radio coverage, traffic, ownership, backhaul, power/backup, damage, availability or restoration; the WFS standard reuse licence is unstated.
The one KNMI Hoogeveen station value is a dated point observation and is not automatically a municipality-wide field or T+72 forecast.
No assigned Waterinfo observation/forecast or RIVM PM2.5 point means bounded point NoData, not normal water, clean air or safety.
NWB, ProRail and GTFS are static geometry/schedule context and do not establish incident road, rail, bus, evacuation, fire, care or logistics continuity; logical route ceilings are scenario units.
The announced N381/A28 closure begins after audit completion and is valid-time planning context; it must not close an arbitrary exercise without matching dates, nor imply post-expiry continuity.
Zero in-boundary RIVM SEH points means no registered questionnaire location, not no local health care, no patients or guaranteed external acute-care availability.
WZA/Treant public service roles do not establish incident occupancy, acceptance, staffing, ambulance travel, diversion, medicines, power/water, generator fuel or backup endurance.
DUO education locations and ordinary municipality/care/recreation facilities do not establish command, shelter, reception or distribution roles.
The 14 March 2026 Eleveld/Geelbroek event and reported possible damage are historical event evidence, not current shaking, future probability or proof that any particular building is damaged/unsafe.
The canonical wildfire lacks local ignition/perimeter/fuel/plume/resource evidence; cyber lacks a named target/architecture/detection; compound combines unvalidated assumptions.

ETP/Attero regulatory, waste and odor context does not establish current toxic exposure, a complete hazardous inventory, live plume, process state or emergency threshold; odor is not equivalent to toxicity.

Nature/recreation visitors, pupils, patients, industrial/agricultural workers, station users, through traffic, responders and external evacuees are not represented by resident population or generic service weights.
Drenthe's support-point planning and Westerveld pilot do not establish a GM1731 support point, capacity, stock, water, power, staff, accessibility or activation.
Household 72-hour preparedness, stocks and ability to assist are not measured; 72 hours is an operations horizon, not guaranteed aid or recovery.

Event-attributable person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not measured customer outage-hours, simultaneous deprivation, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints miss fast fire, release, quake, water-control and medical decisions, and 72 hours excludes prolonged recovery.
